verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents row-level, policy-based authorization: its auth token scopes database access row by row when paired with Postgres RLS policies. Custom claims can be injected via the Custom Access Token Hook, and community users report building on RLS enforcement. However, the evidence is a thin documentation mention tied to RLS, with no dedicated policy engine or relationship-based (ReBAC) model, and one community member looked for an external AuthZ provider. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of policy authoring, relationship-based authorization model, authorization outside Postgres RLS, independent hands-on corroboration of fine-grained policy depth.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can express fine-grained, resource-level authorization (relationship- or policy-based) beyond simple roles

citations.quote: The Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with [RLS policies](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security).
You can use a [Custom Access Token Hook](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) to add, remove or change claims present in the token.
